key_insight: A causal reinforcement learning multimodal model can combine chest X-rays with physician-written histories to improve both MACE risk prediction and reasoning quality.
clinical_relevance: This approach suggests opportunistic screening could use routinely collected imaging and clinical context to help identify patients at elevated cardiovascular risk before an event occurs.
method: Separates reasoning from risk prediction with a role-decoupled dual-LLM design.
Uses a dual-action causal reinforcement learning policy to select evidence and refine reasoning.
Applies causal token pruning to build compact multimodal representations.
evidence_signal: In internal, emergency department, and external MIMIC evaluations, the model outperformed baselines and reported AUROCs of 0.720, 0.760, and 0.845, respectively, with better GREEN scores and expert preference.
watch_item: Performance was shown in retrospective cohorts, so prospective validation and careful workflow integration are needed before clinical use.
paper_title: From Image Interpretation to Clinical Reasoning: Upstream Physician-Context-Aware Multimodal Learning with Causal Reinforcement Learning
